source.title: The Data Efficiency Frontier of Financial Foundation Models: Scaling Laws from Continued Pretraining

record.file_problem: The text is complete, but the referenced figures are not visually present, so plotted values cannot be read.
record.tranche_reason: Tests loss-versus-token scaling in the new setting of continued pretraining on SEC filings, rather than general pretraining from scratch.
record.gate_note: The study reports SEC validation-loss trends and power-law fits for its own DAPT runs. It projects token needs for 7B–70B models but does not train or evaluate those models; these projections do not test predictive accuracy. Downstream evaluation is deferred. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of SEC-domain validation loss against tokens during continued pretraining of Llama-3.2-1B and 3B. That is a test of whether the power-law form holds in a new training regime (V5). It is not a test of from-scratch pretraining loss scaling (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also attribute the shallow exponents to the regularity of SEC text rather than to limits of DAPT. They claim the log-log trend is 'predictable' and extrapolate to 7B–70B token needs, without testing those extrapolations.
record.recipe_differences: This is continued pretraining of existing Llama-3.2 models on a narrow SEC corpus, measured across token checkpoints. It does not perform the broad model/data/compute sweeps or compute-optimal allocation analysis of the original scaling-law studies.

fits_no_version.finding: General-domain (Wikipedia) validation loss stays effectively constant, with variation of about 0.01, over 400M SEC tokens of continued pretraining. The data-efficiency frontier shows SEC gains with negligible general-loss change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow-domain continued pretraining at modest token budgets improves domain loss without measurable general-domain forgetting.

record.problems: Only two model sizes and a single SEC corpus are tested, over a 50M–400M token range. Exact validation losses and fitted exponents are not supplied in the text, and the referenced figures are unavailable here. There are no formal uncertainty estimates or downstream task evaluations. Larger-model token requirements are extrapolations without larger-model runs.

untested.parts: From-scratch pretraining loss scaling in parameters, tokens or compute is not tested. Only continued pretraining over <1 decade of tokens is run, plus two model sizes with no fit.
The 7B–70B token requirements in Table 1 are projections only; no larger run checks them.
Other modalities, repeated data, and fine-tuning/transfer beyond SEC continued pretraining are not tested. A wide token range is not tested.
No downstream evaluation; the authors defer it to future work.
Fitting choices, schedules and data are not varied. Only a fixed learning rate with no scheduler is used.

missing.what: The 3B model has lower SEC loss than the 1B model at every token milestone. This is a two-point parameter comparison with no fit, so it is a weak, non-quantitative bearing on parameter scaling.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author preprint. It has two models, one corpus, and a fixed learning rate with no scheduler. Figures are not available and no numeric exponents are given. The token range is 50M–400M, just under one order of magnitude, so it gives little evidence of power-law form versus other curves. The noted flattening after ~250–300M tokens is not assessed against the fit. Table 1 is a projection and must not be treated as a V2 test.

versions.untested_parts: Parameter-count and compute scaling are not swept; the token range is 50M–400M, not several orders of magnitude.
No larger runs are evaluated against predictions from smaller runs; 7B–70B token requirements are projections only.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation sweep or compute-optimal split is tested.
Depth, width, and architecture details are not varied.
Only text-domain continued pretraining on SEC filings is tested, not other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream task performance is evaluated.
The study does not vary parameter counting, schedules, data, fitting method, or other choices to test fit dependence or curve bending.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Fit SEC-domain validation loss as a function of additional SEC tokens during continued pretraining.
rows.measure: SEC-domain validation loss versus tokens seen; log-log power-law fit
rows.value: Loss decreases smoothly, with the largest improvements between 50M and 200M tokens and a flattening trend beyond roughly 250M–300M. The log-log plot is described as clearly linear; fitted exponent is shallow (|b| ≪ 1).
rows.note: No exact loss values or fitted exponent are given in the text; the range is under one order of magnitude.
rows.check: V1 concerns held-out pretraining loss over several orders of magnitude. This row is continued pretraining over 50M–400M tokens (under one decade), so it belongs to V5 only. The authors describe the log-log trend as 'clear linear', so the form is observed, but no exponent or loss values are given.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Measured general-domain validation loss across continued-pretraining token budgets.
rows.value: Effectively constant across token budgets, with variation on the order of 0.01 and no upward drift reported.
rows.uncertainty: Variation described as within expected noise; no formal uncertainty estimate stated.
rows.note: This is out-of-domain stability during SEC adaptation, not a matched-distribution test of the claimed loss-scaling law.

relationships.condition: Continued pretraining of Llama-3.2-1B and 3B on 400M SEC tokens, 50M–400M token checkpoints
relationships.reason: SEC validation loss is described as log-log linear with shallow exponents for both models (r1, r2). The evidence is weak: under one decade of tokens, and no exponents or losses are reported.
relationships.display_finding: Both models' validation losses are described as log-log linear with shallow exponents across less than one decade of tokens, without reported exponents or loss values.
